body.statement: For \(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\), can \(H_{\mathrm{occ}}\) construct one finite family \(\{Q_t:t\in\mathcal G_r\}\) on the full class \(\mathcal M_H\) such that \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|Q_t(D_n)-Q_t(D_n')|\le1\) for every \(t\), \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\), and \(C_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is independent of the Hölder-sieve dimension, uniformly over all values of \(n\ell^d\)?
body.justification: This is the genuine construction problem: the occupancy identity must survive profiling over every unknown propensity and outcome-regression nuisance without an entropy payment.
body.gap: The downgraded parent reaches only a sparse shared-sign family, while Asi et al. and Chaudhuri et al. do not provide nuisance-independent composite CATE fiber scores.
body.consumer: An affirmative answer combines with the shell proposition and the same-class lower bound to settle the pure-private pointwise-CATE frontier.
